name: Esther Leon

bio.statement: León's voters' pamphlet statement lists her occupation as physical therapist and community college professor.
León's pamphlet statement lists a BA in kinesiology and nutrition from Whittier College and a doctorate in physical therapy from the University of Southern California.
bio.excerpt: Whittier College, BA in Kinesiology & Nutrition; University of Southern California, Doctorate in Physical Therapy

bio.statement: OPB reports León is a physical therapist who works in Oregon prisons and qualifies for the city's donation-matching program.
bio.excerpt: Esther León is a physical therapist who works in Oregon prisons and is also qualified for the donation-matching program.

positions.statement: León's voters' pamphlet statement calls for a vacancy tax on corporate landlords to fund affordable housing.
positions.excerpt: Implement a vacancy tax on corporate landlords that funnels into affordable housing

positions.statement: León's pamphlet statement calls for fully funding Portland Street Response for 24/7 citywide dispatch.
positions.excerpt: Full funding of Portland Street Response for 24/7, city-wide dispatch

positions.statement: León's pamphlet statement calls for a moratorium on AI data centers.
León's pamphlet statement proposes exploring universal basic income for artists.
positions.excerpt: Invest in the Arts: explore universal basic income for artists

positions.statement: León's pamphlet statement calls for fully auditing use of public dollars and holding mishandlers accountable.
positions.excerpt: Fully audit use of public dollars; hold mishandlers accountable

positions.statement: León's pamphlet statement calls for revoking the ICE facility permit, framing it as standing up to fascism.
positions.excerpt: Stand up to fascism: revoke the ICE facility permit

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, León says the city should look at raising the Portland Clean Energy Fund surcharge by another 1%.
positions.excerpt: We should look at raising the PCEF surcharge by another 1%

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Spelling: the county Ballot Content RCV report and inventory print 'Esther Leon'; the county pamphlet index, filing form, OPB and Mercury print 'Esther León'.
